---
title: "GO Hierarchy Check of Transition-Specific Terms"
subtitle: "Are terms significant in only one group related to terms significant in another? (reviewer R2.9)"
---

## Overview

Reviewer R2.9 asked whether GO terms reported as unique to one dementia group could be hierarchically related to terms significant in another group. This notebook takes the saved GO biological-process (BP) enrichment results — no enrichment is re-run — reproduces the manuscript's transition-specific terms (adjusted *P* ≤ 0.05 in exactly one group), and uses the GO graph in `GO.db` to test whether any ancestor or descendant of each such term is significant in a different group. It then reports the result for the functional categories the Results and Discussion rely on, and repeats the group-level count at the top 2,000 CpG sites.

Since 2026-10-09 the terms follow the authors' recount: parent terms whose genes are identical to those of a significant child are dropped first (Rule 1, from `03_go_term_weights.qmd`), and the manuscript reports specificity weights based on immediate relatives (Rule 2, same notebook) instead of this any-ancestor-or-descendant check, which stays as the internal record.

## Load packages

`GO.db` supplies the GO BP graph and `readxl` reads the saved functional categories; the tidyverse and `here` are pre-loaded by `.Rprofile`.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages

pacman::p_load(GO.db, readxl, install = FALSE)

conflicted::conflict_prefer_all("dplyr", quiet = TRUE)

source(here("custom_func/assign_biofunc_category.R"))
source(here("custom_func/go_term_weights.R"))
```

## Helper functions

Small helpers that read the significant terms, apply the manuscript's transition-specific definition, walk the GO graph and collect each unique term's significant relatives in other groups.

```{r}
#| label: helpers

group_levels <- c("normal2mci", "stable_mci", "normal2incid", "mci2incid", "prev")

# Significant GO BP terms per group, as in 03_transition_specific_GO_terms (duplicate parents dropped)
read_sig_terms <- function(top_n) {
  read_rds(here(glue("pathway_analysis/02_gene_ontology/output/top{top_n}_all_GO_results.rds"))) |>
    dplyr::filter(p.adjust <= 0.05, !ID %in% read_go_duplicate_parents(top_n)$parent) |>
    dplyr::select(condition, ID, Description)
}

# Manuscript definition: significant in exactly one group, counted by GO ID
get_unique_terms <- function(sig_terms) {
  sig_terms |>
    add_count(ID, name = "n_GO") |>
    dplyr::filter(n_GO == 1) |>
    dplyr::select(-n_GO)
}

# Ancestors of one term by breadth-first walk over GOBPPARENTS, optionally
# restricted to some edge types ("isa", "part of", "regulates", ...)
bp_parents <- as.list(GOBPPARENTS)

walk_ancestors <- function(id, relations = NULL) {
  found <- character()
  frontier <- id
  while (length(frontier) > 0) {
    edges <- unlist(unname(bp_parents[frontier]))
    if (!is.null(relations)) edges <- edges[names(edges) %in% relations]
    new_ids <- setdiff(unique(unname(edges)), c(found, "all"))
    found <- c(found, new_ids)
    frontier <- new_ids
  }
  found
}

# Direct GO edges (parents or children) of a set of terms, with their edge type
direct_edges <- function(bimap, term_ids, direction) {
  as.list(bimap[term_ids]) |>
    map(\(x) tibble(rel_id = unname(x), relation = names(x))) |>
    list_rbind(names_to = "term_id") |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(rel_id)) |>
    mutate(direction = direction)
}

# Every (unique term, relative) pair in which the relative is an ancestor or
# descendant of the unique term and is significant in a DIFFERENT group
find_cross_group_relatives <- function(sig_terms, unique_terms) {
  term_ids <- unique_terms$ID

  all_relatives <- bind_rows(
    as.list(GOBPANCESTOR[term_ids]) |>
      enframe("term_id", "rel_id") |>
      unnest_longer(rel_id) |>
      mutate(direction = "ancestor"),
    as.list(GOBPOFFSPRING[term_ids]) |>
      enframe("term_id", "rel_id") |>
      unnest_longer(rel_id) |>
      mutate(direction = "descendant")
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(rel_id), rel_id != "all")

  direct <- bind_rows(
    direct_edges(GOBPPARENTS, term_ids, "ancestor"),
    direct_edges(GOBPCHILDREN, term_ids, "descendant")
  ) |>
    summarise(
      relation = str_c(sort(unique(relation)), collapse = "; "),
      .by = c(term_id, rel_id, direction)
    )

  strict_ancestors <- unique(sig_terms$ID) |>
    set_names() |>
    map(\(id) walk_ancestors(id, relations = c("isa", "part of")))

  all_relatives |>
    inner_join(
      unique_terms |>
        dplyr::rename(term_id = ID, term_condition = condition, term_description = Description),
      by = "term_id"
    ) |>
    inner_join(
      sig_terms |>
        dplyr::rename(rel_id = ID, rel_condition = condition, rel_description = Description),
      by = "rel_id",
      relationship = "many-to-many"
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(rel_condition != term_condition) |>
    left_join(direct, by = c("term_id", "rel_id", "direction")) |>
    mutate(
      direct = !is.na(relation),
      isa_partof = map2_lgl(
        term_id, rel_id,
        \(t, r) r %in% strict_ancestors[[t]] || t %in% strict_ancestors[[r]]
      )
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(
      term_condition, term_id, term_description, direction, direct, relation,
      isa_partof, rel_condition, rel_id, rel_description
    )
}

# One row per unique term, flagging the kind of cross-group relative it has
summarise_terms <- function(unique_terms, relatives) {
  per_term <- relatives |>
    summarise(
      n_relatives = n_distinct(rel_id),
      has_ancestor = any(direction == "ancestor"),
      has_descendant = any(direction == "descendant"),
      has_direct = any(direct),
      has_isa_partof = any(isa_partof),
      relative_groups = str_c(sort(unique(rel_condition)), collapse = ", "),
      relatives = str_c(unique(glue("{rel_description} [{rel_condition}]")), collapse = "; "),
      .by = term_id
    )

  unique_terms |>
    left_join(per_term, by = c(ID = "term_id")) |>
    mutate(
      has_relative = !is.na(n_relatives),
      n_relatives = replace_na(n_relatives, 0L),
      across(c(has_ancestor, has_descendant, has_direct, has_isa_partof), \(x) replace_na(x, FALSE))
    )
}

# Per-group counts plus a total row
summarise_groups <- function(term_hierarchy, top_n) {
  by_group <- term_hierarchy |>
    summarise(
      n_unique = n(),
      n_with_relative = sum(has_relative, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_via_ancestor = sum(has_ancestor, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_via_descendant = sum(has_descendant, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_via_direct = sum(has_direct, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_isa_partof = sum(has_isa_partof, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = condition
    ) |>
    arrange(factor(condition, levels = group_levels))

  by_group |>
    bind_rows(
      by_group |>
        summarise(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
        mutate(condition = "total")
    ) |>
    mutate(
      top_n = top_n,
      n_without_relative = n_unique - n_with_relative,
      pct_with_relative = n_with_relative / n_unique,
      .after = condition
    ) |>
    relocate(top_n)
}
```

## Reproduce the transition-specific terms

The significant BP terms per group and the unique set are rebuilt from the saved enrichment results with the same rule as `03_transition_specific_GO_terms`, and checked against the counts quoted in the Results and against that step's saved CSV.

```{r}
#| label: reproduce-top1000

sig_1000 <- read_sig_terms(1000)
unique_1000 <- get_unique_terms(sig_1000)

sig_counts <- sig_1000 |> count(condition)
unique_counts <- unique_1000 |> count(condition)

stopifnot(
  identical(
    deframe(sig_counts)[group_levels],
    c(normal2mci = 152L, stable_mci = 12L, normal2incid = 16L, mci2incid = 48L, prev = 22L)
  ),
  nrow(unique_1000) == 204,
  # the manuscript's saved transition-specific set
  setequal(
    unique_1000$ID,
    read_csv(
      here("pathway_analysis/03_transition_specific_GO_terms/output/top1000_condition_specific_GO_terms.csv"),
      show_col_types = FALSE
    )$ID
  ),
  # every significant term is in the installed GO graph
  all(sig_1000$ID %in% keys(GOBPANCESTOR))
)

sig_counts |>
  left_join(unique_counts |> dplyr::rename(n_unique = n), by = "condition") |>
  arrange(factor(condition, levels = group_levels)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Significant and transition-specific GO BP terms, top 1,000 CpG sites")
```

The installed GO graph is `GO.db` `r packageVersion("GO.db")`, built from the GO release of `r GO_dbInfo() |> dplyr::filter(name == "GOSOURCEDATE") |> pull(value)`.

## Check the GO graph helpers

The breadth-first walk over all edge types must reproduce `GOBPANCESTOR` exactly, which validates the walker used for the stricter `is_a`/`part_of`-only check. `GOBPANCESTOR` follows `regulates` edges as well, so "regulation of X" counts as related to "X" in the primary analysis.

```{r}
#| label: check-walker

walker_agrees <- unique(sig_1000$ID) |>
  map_lgl(\(id) setequal(walk_ancestors(id), setdiff(GOBPANCESTOR[[id]], "all")))

stopifnot(all(walker_agrees))

bp_parents[unique(sig_1000$ID)] |>
  unname() |>
  unlist() |>
  names() |>
  tibble(relation = _) |>
  count(relation, name = "n_edges") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Edge types from the significant terms to their direct parents")
```

## Cross-group hierarchical relatives at top 1,000

For each of the 204 transition-specific terms, all GO ancestors and descendants are looked up and kept only when that relative is significant in a different group.

```{r}
#| label: relatives-top1000

relatives_1000 <- find_cross_group_relatives(sig_1000, unique_1000)

term_hierarchy_1000 <- summarise_terms(unique_1000, relatives_1000)
group_summary_1000 <- summarise_groups(term_hierarchy_1000, 1000)

group_summary_1000 |>
  mutate(pct_with_relative = scales::percent(pct_with_relative, accuracy = 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Transition-specific terms with an ancestor or descendant significant in another group (top 1,000)")
```

### Which groups the relatives come from

Each unique term is counted once per other group in which it has a significant relative, so a term can appear in more than one column.

```{r}
#| label: group-crosstab

relatives_1000 |>
  distinct(term_condition, term_id, rel_condition) |>
  count(term_condition, rel_condition) |>
  mutate(
    term_condition = factor(term_condition, levels = group_levels),
    rel_condition = factor(rel_condition, levels = group_levels)
  ) |>
  arrange(term_condition, rel_condition) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = rel_condition, values_from = n, values_fill = 0, names_sort = TRUE) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Unique terms (rows: their group) with a significant relative in each other group (columns)")
```

### Direct parent/child relatives

These are the pairs in which the relative is an immediate GO parent or child of the unique term, with the edge type joining them.

```{r}
#| label: direct-pairs

relatives_1000 |>
  dplyr::filter(direct) |>
  arrange(factor(term_condition, levels = group_levels), term_description) |>
  dplyr::select(term_condition, term_description, direction, relation, rel_condition, rel_description) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Unique terms whose direct GO parent or child is significant in another group")
```

## Functional categories

The functional categories are read from the saved output of `04_function_categorization` and confirmed against `assign_biofunc_category()`; each cross-group relative is categorised with the same function to show whether it would fall in the same category.

```{r}
#| label: categories

categories_1000 <- read_excel(
  here("pathway_analysis/04_function_categorization/output/top1000_condition_specific_GO_terms_auto_cat.xlsx")
)

stopifnot(
  setequal(categories_1000$ID, unique_1000$ID),
  identical(assign_biofunc_category(categories_1000$Description), categories_1000$function_category)
)

same_category_terms <- relatives_1000 |>
  left_join(categories_1000 |> dplyr::select(ID, function_category), by = c(term_id = "ID")) |>
  mutate(rel_category = assign_biofunc_category(rel_description)) |>
  dplyr::filter(coalesce(rel_category == function_category, FALSE)) |>
  distinct(term_id) |>
  pull(term_id)

term_hierarchy_1000 <- term_hierarchy_1000 |>
  left_join(categories_1000 |> dplyr::select(ID, function_category), by = "ID") |>
  mutate(has_same_category_relative = ID %in% same_category_terms) |>
  relocate(function_category, .after = Description)
```

### Categories cited in the Results and Discussion

These are the categories the text describes as specific to one group; the table gives how many of each category's terms have a hierarchical relative significant elsewhere, and how many of those relatives would be assigned to the same category.

```{r}
#| label: focal-categories

focal_categories <- tribble(
  ~condition,     ~function_category,
  "normal2mci",   "Ion Transport and Regulation",
  "normal2mci",   "Synaptic Function and Organization",
  "normal2mci",   "Extracellular Matrix Organization",
  "normal2mci",   "Immune Response",
  "normal2mci",   "Glial Cell Regulation",
  "stable_mci",   "Hypoxia Response",
  "stable_mci",   "Regulatory Mechanisms",
  "normal2incid", "Synaptic Vesicle Control",
  "mci2incid",    "Hormone Signaling",
  "mci2incid",    "Cell Migration and Organization",
  "prev",         "Cell Cycle Regulation"
)

focal_category_hierarchy <- focal_categories |>
  left_join(
    term_hierarchy_1000 |>
      summarise(
        n_terms = n(),
        n_with_relative = sum(has_relative, na.rm = TRUE),
        n_via_direct = sum(has_direct, na.rm = TRUE),
        n_isa_partof = sum(has_isa_partof, na.rm = TRUE),
        n_same_category_relative = sum(has_same_category_relative, na.rm = TRUE),
        .by = c(condition, function_category)
      ),
    by = c("condition", "function_category")
  ) |>
  mutate(n_without_relative = n_terms - n_with_relative, .after = n_with_relative)

stopifnot(
  identical(
    focal_category_hierarchy$n_terms,
    c(13L, 8L, 7L, 7L, 3L, 3L, 2L, 4L, 5L, 7L, 3L)
  )
)

focal_category_hierarchy |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Focal functional categories: terms with a hierarchical relative significant in another group (top 1,000)")
```

### Focal-category terms that have a relative elsewhere

The individual terms behind the table above, with their relatives and the group in which each relative is significant.

```{r}
#| label: focal-terms

term_hierarchy_1000 |>
  semi_join(focal_categories, by = c("condition", "function_category")) |>
  dplyr::filter(has_relative) |>
  arrange(factor(condition, levels = group_levels), function_category, Description) |>
  dplyr::select(condition, function_category, Description, has_direct, has_same_category_relative, relatives) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Focal-category terms with a significant relative in another group")
```

## Secondary check at top 2,000

The same group-level count is repeated for the top 2,000 CpG sites; functional categories are not re-examined here.

```{r}
#| label: top2000

sig_2000 <- read_sig_terms(2000)
unique_2000 <- get_unique_terms(sig_2000)

stopifnot(
  setequal(
    unique_2000$ID,
    read_csv(
      here("pathway_analysis/03_transition_specific_GO_terms/output/top2000_condition_specific_GO_terms.csv"),
      show_col_types = FALSE
    )$ID
  ),
  all(sig_2000$ID %in% keys(GOBPANCESTOR))
)

relatives_2000 <- find_cross_group_relatives(sig_2000, unique_2000)
term_hierarchy_2000 <- summarise_terms(unique_2000, relatives_2000)
group_summary_2000 <- summarise_groups(term_hierarchy_2000, 2000)

sig_2000 |>
  count(condition) |>
  left_join(unique_2000 |> count(condition, name = "n_unique"), by = "condition") |>
  arrange(factor(condition, levels = group_levels)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Significant and transition-specific GO BP terms, top 2,000 CpG sites")

group_summary_2000 |>
  mutate(pct_with_relative = scales::percent(pct_with_relative, accuracy = 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Transition-specific terms with an ancestor or descendant significant in another group (top 2,000)")
```

## Save the results

Tidy tables are saved as `.rds` for the response letter: pair-level relatives and term-level flags at top 1,000, the focal-category table, and the group summaries at both thresholds.

```{r}
#| label: save

out_dir <- here("pathway_analysis/06_go_hierarchy/output")
fs::dir_create(out_dir)

write_rds(relatives_1000, fs::path(out_dir, "top1000_unique_term_relatives.rds"))
write_rds(term_hierarchy_1000, fs::path(out_dir, "top1000_unique_term_hierarchy.rds"))
write_rds(focal_category_hierarchy, fs::path(out_dir, "top1000_focal_category_hierarchy.rds"))
write_rds(
  bind_rows(group_summary_1000, group_summary_2000),
  fs::path(out_dir, "hierarchy_summary_by_group.rds")
)
```

## Summary

The key numbers for the response to R2.9, computed above.

```{r}
#| label: summary-numbers

total_1000 <- group_summary_1000 |> dplyr::filter(condition == "total")
total_2000 <- group_summary_2000 |> dplyr::filter(condition == "total")
n2m_1000 <- group_summary_1000 |> dplyr::filter(condition == "normal2mci")
```

At the top 1,000 CpG sites, `r total_1000$n_with_relative` of the `r total_1000$n_unique` transition-specific GO BP terms (`r scales::percent(total_1000$pct_with_relative, accuracy = 1)`) had at least one GO ancestor or descendant that was significant in another group, and `r total_1000$n_via_direct` of these had such a relative as a direct parent or child. Restricting the GO graph to `is_a` and `part_of` edges, `r total_1000$n_isa_partof` terms had such a relative. The remaining `r total_1000$n_without_relative` terms had no significant relative in any other group. For normal2mci, `r n2m_1000$n_with_relative` of `r n2m_1000$n_unique` unique terms had a relative elsewhere (`r n2m_1000$n_via_direct` through a direct parent or child).

At the top 2,000 CpG sites, `r total_2000$n_with_relative` of `r total_2000$n_unique` transition-specific terms (`r scales::percent(total_2000$pct_with_relative, accuracy = 1)`) had a significant relative in another group.
